To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of fungi as biocatalyst in gas-phase biofiltration is a promising alternative to bacteria.
fungal biocatalyst strains are able to degrade alkene and aromatic hydrocarbons in biofilters, with high elimination capacity and high resistance to adverse conditions.

the fungal biocatalyst is able to degrade alkane-, alkene-, alkene-, and alkylbenzene-related VOCs and that the elimination capacities reached are 10-20 times higher than those obtained with the best bacterial strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new biocatalysts for the biofiltraton of VOC-pollutated air.

the isolation and selection of new fungal strains, their use as biodegrading biocatalysts, and the study of the factors that control their performance in the biofiltrations of volatile organic compounds.
the development of new fungal strains able as biocatalyst in the gas-phase biotreatment of air polluted with volatile organic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

fungal strains have a great potential to become biocatalysts for the biofiltrations of hydrophobic volatile organic pollutants, although further research is needed to better understand and optimize the biofiltration process.
fungal biofilters are a promising alternative to conventional biofilters for the removal of hydrophobic pollutants from air.
fungal strains can play a major role in the development of new and improved biofilters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fungal biocatalyst is a promising candidate for the treatment of VOC-pollutants in gas-phase biofiltration.
fungal strains are promising biocatalysts for the biofiltrations of VOC-pollutant.
fungal biocatalyst are very promising for the treatment of air polluted with hydrophobic VOCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the search for efficient fungal strains able to grow on the carrier material of the biofilter and to degrade volatile organic pollutants is still a major challenge for the future.

fungi have a potential as biocatalyst in gas-phase biofiltration and that further research is necessary in order to fully understand their behavior in this kind of bioreactors and to improve their performance.
the use of fungal biofilms as biocatalyst in biofilters is a promising approach for air pollution abatement.
